items.stem: A team's Project returns answers that mix two unrelated engagements. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Unrelated files for both engagements are loaded in the same Project
options.rationale: Correct: mixing unrelated material in one Project degrades retrieval relevance.

options.text: The team has too few members
options.rationale: Member count does not cause content mixing.
The problem is scoping of the knowledge, not file reading.
Chat length does not explain cross-engagement mixing.

items.explanation: Correct: mixing unrelated material in one Project degrades retrieval relevance.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO belong in a shared team Project's instructions? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The house style and citation convention
options.rationale: Correct: shared conventions keep every member's chats consistent.
Transient content does not belong in persistent project instructions.
Correct: a clear purpose steers retrieval and keeps the Project focused.
Credentials must never be placed in shared instructions.

items.explanation: Correct: shared conventions keep every member's chats consistent.

items.stem: Which task is the clearest fit for a one-off chat rather than a Project?

options.text: Quickly rephrasing a single sentence with no reuse or shared context
options.rationale: Correct: a trivial, non-recurring task needs no persistent shared workspace.

options.text: A six-week research engagement with shared files
options.rationale: That needs the persistence of a Project.

options.text: A team knowledge base updated weekly
options.rationale: Ongoing shared knowledge belongs in a Project.
Shared, controlled access points to a Project.

items.explanation: Correct: a trivial, non-recurring task needs no persistent shared workspace.
